newsitem.title: KUWAIT: New Saudi "terrorist" attacks averted, Perry says.
newsitem.headline: New Saudi "terrorist" attacks averted, Perry says.

text.p: U.S. and Saudi Arabian intelligence efforts averted possible new "terrorist" attacks in the kingdom and the American military remains on high alert there, U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Thursday.

Perry told reporters flying with him from Bosnia to Kuwait on a Gulf visit that will also take him to Saudi Arabia on Friday that there had been a number of arrests to prevent possible attacks in the kingdom.
He said anonymous terrorist threats were received weekly but declined to give details.
A total of 24 U.S. soldiers were killed in two bomb attacks in Saudi Arabia in November, 1995, and in June of this year. Investigations continue into those incidents.

"These are cases where I cannot discuss details," Perry said of the averted attacks. "They were based on intelligence information we or the Saudis had. Based on that information, either they or we took action and it, in our judgement, averted what would have been some sort of a terrorist attempted action."
"Yes," he told reporters aboard his aircraft when asked if arrests were made.
He said anonymous threats were received by the Saudis or the U.S. military "at least once a week", and while many may be harassment or hoaxes, they were taken seriously.
"One of the consequences of that is we are still on a high threat alert in Saudi Arabia," he said.
Perry was asked about published reports from Dubai this week that a radical Islamic group threatened to attack U.S. forces in Saudi Arabia unless jailed Moslem militants were freed.
The statement from the Movement for Islamic Change was the second since a June 25 truck bomb of a U.S. military housing complex in eastern Saudi Arabia in which 19 U.S. troops died.
Since that attack, the U.S. military has moved nearly 4,000 of its air force personnel to a remote Prince Sultan Air Base in the desert and is improving security for troops in Riyadh.

"Both we and the Saudis have a very intensive intelligence effort to uncover hard information about what's going on. That information also supports the view that we should remain on a high alert," Perry said.

"From a more positive point of view, it (intelligence) allows us to take action to head off explicit or specific actions that may be planned against us and there have been a few such cases," he added.

The Saudi government executed four Saudi citizens in the first bombing and Saudi authorities and the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation are cooperating in an inquiry into the June 25 blast at the military housing facility at Dhahran.
No culprits have been announced in the second bombing attack although published reports said the Saudis arrested as many as 40 people in connection with the investigation.

Perry will hold meetings with senior Kuwaiti officials on Friday before visiting Qatar and Saudi Arabia and is expected to announce here that the United States is removing 8 F-117A "Stealth" fighters moved to Kuwait in September in a U.S. confrontation with Iraq.
The United States at that time moved more than 3,000 troops to Kuwait and Perry said on Thursday that the troops would be removed in December and "will be home before Christmas".
He told reporters the situation was now quiet in Iraq, where attacks by President Saddam Hussein's army against Kurds in northern Iraq prompted U.S. Cruise missile attacks in September.

Perry said the United States had recently moved a marine amphibious force of 1,800 troops on ships in the Gulf off Kuwait to be ready after army troops leave Kuwait next month. "I don't think you can ever take your eyes off Saddam Hussein," he said.
